memory.expert_advice_followed:
NOTE: This implementation passes trainability checks but deviates from the proposed mathematical spec. The tuner is optimizing an approximation of the intended architecture. Deviations: The model implementation is robust and follows the requested architectural logic. While the Film implementation deviates from the spec (the spec describes a gate driven by [mean c1, mean c2, log n] to output gamma/beta, whereas the implementation uses a linear projection to 4*H then splits, effectively providing a different parameterization), it remains a valid, trainable neural network architecture. Residualisation logic is correctly implemented using masked normal equations, and skip connections for the baseline statistic are properly handled.

Focus areas: Learning rate and epochs: the model is tiny and has only 60 training datasets, so watch overfitting to tile composition.; Ablate the covariate residualisation (on/off) and the skip a*z_p (on/off) first.; Ridge lambda and the number of L-rank bins for the dose-response contrast.; Dropout and weight decay, to limit overfitting to tile-specific cell-type mix.; Recall of weak (beta=0.5) positives, if beta can be inspected offline.
Constraints: VRAM: stay under about 80% of the 6.37 GB effective cap. The pairwise rank comparison costs about B*N*N floats (4 MB per triple at N=1024), so keep batch_size at or below about 64 and chunk the pairwise comparison if raised.; Output must be exactly [B,1], finite, with no NaN when a triple has few or zero contact cells (clamp n, guard atanh and division).; Model must be invariant to column order and must not use batch-level statistics.; No fixed dataset constants and no use of validation labels for fitting any normalisation.
Known failures: Few training datasets with ~7% positives: the MLP may overfit tile-specific composition and fall below the Spearman baseline. Mitigation: the skip connection, a zero-initialised head and small capacity.; Weak positives are nearly indistinguishable from unobserved-ligand perturbation negatives, so upweighting them could add noise. The beta-weighted loss cannot be applied here, because the target contract carries only the 0/1 label.; Residualising on row 3 (sender-neighbour fraction) could remove real signal, because the injected effect is defined over contact cells. Keep a raw-rank path in the per-cell features as a hedge.; smooth_l1 on a 0/1 target with ~7% positives can collapse toward predicting 0. The skip path and ranking-only evaluation mitigate this, but monitor score variance.
Suggested directions: First run the baseline config for about 30 epochs with the cosine schedule and compare validation lr_auprc against the Spearman statistic alone (a fixed, head-disabled variant).; Then ablate residualisation and the per-cell pooled branch to see which supplies the gain.; Then try a small lr sweep (5e-4 to 5e-3) and dropout 0.1 to 0.3.; If weak-effect recall stays low, consider a future custom loss with beta weighting once beta labels can be routed to the loss. This is not possible under the current [B,1] target contract.
Rationale: The task has a strong, known statistical signal (rank dependence of R on neighbour L). The most reliable gains are covariate-adjusted, mask-correct correlation features that are robust to nuisance, with a small learned correction on top. A tiny model with a baseline-initialised skip keeps training fast, as the human requested, and limits overfitting on 60 datasets.
memory.hypothesis: The skip-connected model with a zero-initialised head should match or slightly exceed the Spearman baseline on lr_auprc (well above the ~0.11 random level). The learned correction should add a small gain without overfitting the tile mix.
memory.conclusion: Good (provisional, first scored run): lr_auprc=0.5823 is far above the ~0.11 random level named in the hypothesis, with lr_auroc 0.891 and direction_accuracy 0.806. No baseline or best-so-far score is available, so it is the current best by default (is_new_best=True). I cannot say whether it matches or beats the Spearman baseline, so the 'match or slightly exceed' part of the hypothesis is untested.
memory.key_factor: Skip-connected MLP coupling model with a zero-initialised head (8162 params, smooth_l1, 30 epochs, cosine-decayed lr starting at 0.002). It starts from the Spearman-like baseline and learns a correction on top.
memory.discovery: Training was stable and well generalised. Train smooth_l1 fell 0.236->0.0216 and validation fell 0.0543->0.0220. The final train-val gap was only +0.00033. Validation was best at about epoch 14-15, and the selected checkpoint was epoch 15 (val 0.02189). It then plateaued, drifting only +8e-5 over the last 15 epochs. So there is no overfitting, and the later epochs under the decayed lr added almost nothing. The same capacity would probably work with about 15-20 epochs. The model is small and the gap is tiny, so capacity is not the bottleneck. Gains are more likely to come from the architecture, the input features, or the loss than from longer training. Training ran at the full operator-set formal portion (1.0), so data volume is not a concern.
memory.memory_update: Record lr_auprc=0.5823 (auroc 0.891, dir_acc 0.806) as the first reference for smooth_l1 with the skip-MLP and zero-init head (8162 params, 30 epochs, lr 0.002 cosine, train loss 0.0216, val ~0.0220). Next steps: (1) Run or retrieve the pure Spearman baseline score at the same formal scope. That is needed to see whether the learned correction adds anything over the baseline. (2) Test a efficiency variant with 15-20 epochs, since val plateaued by epoch ~15. If the score stays within 5%, flag it as a high-efficiency candidate. (3) Change one factor at a time to find real gains, for example latent width or depth, or a different loss_type. Do not compare loss values across different loss types. Formal scope is operator-fixed at 1.0, so do not suggest changing trial_portion for formal rounds. Single-seed score differences under a few percent should be treated cautiously.
